title: STREET RATS (wip with UNITY/VS CODE/AFFINITY)
author: SamSampersand
selftext:
Hi all, work in progress sharing:

**Short intro**: 10+ years ago I studied gamedesign at HoWest for a year and got my bachelor in Arts. During my thesis around specifically indiegame design and graphic design in games I layed out the foundation and idea for a 2d arcade game in unity. I pretty soon realised it's a massive mountain to climb, and begged coders and musicians to help out. The only reply I got was 'how much are you willing to pay" and "don't have time". In the end found and paid a coder to create one level and done. However the dream remained...

The passed half year I've shifted from being a strategic digital marketeer and graphic designer to adding Salesforce developer to the list. Writing JavaScript, Ampscript, SQL, SSJS, ...  building API'S, contentpages, and more. I thank Dabrowski for his helpful sources of information. If you read this dear sir, you are a legend.

**Status:** Today with the help of AI I'm giving it another shot, same idea but not needing to depend on others to bring the vision to life. One month in and I'm really vibing ❤️🫟 Even launched the album on Spotify with 14 tracks for the in-game already. Working between 6 to 20 hours per week on it depending on the weather and how much life comes in the picture(\*).

**The workflow** is to let ChatGPT run the code through codex (C#) with clear supervision from my end, myself creating artwork with affinity, putting it in Gemini for faster spritesheet creation (poses) and then back into affinity for clipping the frames and fine-tuning, then working in Unity and making backups through GitHub. Development on Mac OS.

* MVP1 is to have a demo for Unity Steam(deck) windows mac and steamdeck.
* MVP2 Will immediately be go live I think; where the entire level uses the layered spriteboards I have and auto generate levels. Bigger/smaller depending on easy medium or hard mode and autospawn enemies inside it. With unlockable music tracks, graffiti pieces, and a bunch of easter eggs. 

Follow along for the progress on: [https://www.instagram.com/streetratsgame](https://www.instagram.com/streetratsgame)

\-------  
\**PS: Yes, 'only' 6-20 hours per week because I run a thight schedule working full-time,* [*learning to tattoo*](http://www.instagram.com/sinsamtattoo)*, hitting the bicycle/gym because I need to lose 15 to 20 kg and train for bikepacking, and well... my household shores as well* 😂 *Don't let anyone tell you there's not enough time to do the things you dream about doing.*

comments.author: MidnightMiniature
comments.body: Love these kind of games, really nice design! Will definitely follow the project

replies.author: SamSampersand
replies.body: Thanks dude(tte)! It's really a passion project for me.

comments.author: _TofuRious_
comments.body:
The art (specifically animation) is not doing it for me. Might be ok as stills, although still has that very generic AI vibe to it. 
I'm super biased because I come from an animation background so perhaps my eye is a little too attuned to it, but most AI animation i see is pretty dogshit. Horrible weighting, and super linear movement. Completely void of any character. 

But out side of the art, looks pretty solid. Definitely has a retro feel to the game play.

replies.author: SamSampersand
replies.body: Thanks for the input. For sure I'll need to work on anything related to animation. It never quite gets movement the way it should (stepping left foot forward, right foot forward cycle etcetera). In this first stage I want to make everything "work" technically and then focus on anything animation and build out the spritesheet deck.

comments.author: enricokern
comments.body: You see its generated alone from the idle character changing size on animations, typical pixelgen issue. If you are an artist why does it look all generated? (Not an issue with that but curious)

replies.author: SamSampersand
replies.body: I'm embracing a counterintuitive process of making it work first, pretty later. I know the art and animations will not be a problem but will just take a lot of time. Simultaneously I know getting bugs and errors in code still demotivates me. Getting the hard part done first, cancelling the ChatGPT license once I've established the code working; and then I can focus on making all the sprites perfect which will take weeks/months but that's perfectly okay for me.
